newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice deputy mayor praised after fake execution.
newsitem.headline: Venice deputy mayor praised after fake execution.

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro praised the deputy mayor of Venice for his tough stand against crime on Thursday after he was the victim of a fake execution apparently carried out by an organised crime group.

"I would like to express my warmest solidarity with Gianfranco Bettin...the victim of a serious aggression, for his courageous campaign against crime," Scalfaro said in a telegram sent to the mayor of Venice, Massimo Cacciari.
Bettin was getting into his car in the industrial mainland Mestre district on Wednesday evening when a man appeared from the back seat and put a gun to his temple.
Newspapers, which carried lengthy reconstructions of the incident, quoted Bettin as saying he was forced to drive to a deserted spot near Mestre's lagoonside industrial zone.
The man, whom Bettin said had a southern Italian accent, ordered him to stop and throw the car keys out of the window.
"Mr Mayor, you've got to mind your own business," the attacker said. Then he pulled the trigger.
"I thought, he can't really be doing this. Christ. Then I heard "click'," Corriere della Sera quoted Bettin as saying.
"I was paralysed, I couldn't breathe. I could see him in the rear-view mirror. He muttered something like "Next time it'll be loaded' and then he got out."
Bettin, a member of the Greens party, has already received death threats on his answering machine at home and once had a knife put to his throat, La Repubblica reported.

Newspapers said the attack was most likely a warning by a northern branch of the Naples-based Camorra crime group in response to Bettin's campaign to stem its infiltration of some neighbourhoods in Mestre.
